record_notes.DCP-LETT-2003: November 26, supplied 1856; all six blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Asks Bentham about trees with enclosed papilionaceous reproductive parts, tentative inferences from Loudon woodcuts and frequency of natural crossing. Robinia observation deferred to next summer; questions about polygamy and crosses not results. Explicitly uncertain guide and wild speculation retained. No apetalous-flower question here as specific as the later November 30 follow-up.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2005: November 30, supplied 1856; all four blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing Bentham answer and retracts assumption few trees have papilionaceous flowers. Recalls older conversation on apetalous plants and asks for names, authority to quote, and British examples to watch. Almost without anthers does not mean no pollen. Proposed explanation via transported pollen or agamic seeding is conditional, not established. Future quotation does not imply it appeared in Natural selection or Origin; apparatus says none did. Same-author 2003 is not incoming prompt. December 2 surviving response answers this new question.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-11267: December 2, supplied 1856; all five blocks, six notes and separate Darwin annotations read; no bibliography section. Bentham lists particular apetalous legume cases with almost but not quite no anthers, retracts prior Arachis/Stylosanthes claim and warns against quoting those as examples. British violets explicitly answer November 30 request, with Russian violet observation and different early/late flowering order from Ononis. Other families have exposed stamens, distinction preserved. Darwin So not coincident annotation undated. Raw Martia in the Neurocarpum discussion and footnote Viola martia identification are not silently harmonised; source edition taxonomic gloss remains separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2010: December 3, supplied 1856; both body blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Explicitly thanks apetalous-flower information and says too exceptional to help. Russian violets to be obtained and watched next summer; not already observed. Prior heartsease/bee observations are Darwin additional evidence, not supplied by Bentham. Source spells Heartease; later study not imported.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2177: December 1, supplied 1857; all seven blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing note on naturalised clover and spreading plants. Westward movement and European agricultural adaptation discussed as speculation, not tested victory of weeds. Silene list given to Hooker for Bentham classification, author names missing in Gartner. Permission to quote desired. Book regarded hypothetical with serious difficulties. Poppy competition hypothetical, foreign seed case in later book not complete incoming reconstruction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2184: December 15, supplied 1857; all four blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Adds Cucubalus list overlooked after Silene list, asks pair-by-pair species/variety classification and permission to cite. Aim is compare near-perfect cross fertility with disagreements about species; undisputed distinct species not relevant to that argument, not a request to falsify results. Lists not themselves reproduced here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2186: Supplied December 16 or 17, 1857; all three surviving blocks, two notes and bibliography read. Damaged letter returns both lists and warns garden names may not identify intended species. Describes Silene substitutions and distinctions with genuine gaps retained. Metadata describes two damaged Darwin lists with Bentham notes and another Darwin note, but raw letter contains only body, footnotes and bibliography: full annotated lists absent, no enclosure section or actual figures. Return of lists demonstrated, detailed rows cannot be reconstructed from metadata. Composition constrained between December 15 request and December 18 response, not exact receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2189: December 18, supplied 1857; all three blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Explicit thanks for answers and adoption of identification caveat. Cucubalus viscosus/Italicus extreme sterility contrasted with other forms nearly fertile; effect of manipulation on slight reduction remains Darwin conjecture. Gartner cowslip/primrose and Anagallis examples are reported prior experiments, not Darwin own completed trial. Reply to surviving cover identified, but detailed other-form results also depend on missing returned lists.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1830: February 7, 1856, damaged six-page ALS; all four long surviving blocks, thirteen notes, separate annotations and bibliography read. Bunbury compares Lindley reported Colletia garden transformation with Hooker description and his uncle Henry Stephen Fox herbarium specimens, not William Darwin Fox. Seed origin explicitly unsatisfactory, not established transmutation. Report that Darwin supports unlimited mutability is hearsay that Bunbury doubts; his own openness to wider variation stops short of unlimited change. Cape taxa and identity uncertainties, numerical species contrasts and damage preserved. Body Duval, summary Dunal, and footnote potato-work description versus listed Histoire du pommier are inconsistent apparatus; do not silently settle identity from these alone. Letter physically cut into two for Darwin portfolios, filing marks undated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1854: April 16, 1856 incomplete letter; all seven surviving blocks, nine notes, full Darwin annotations and bibliography read. Responds to missing Darwin letter received upwards of two months earlier; no precise day inferred. P2 quotes Joseph Hooker reply about Colletia and then gives Bunbury inference about Lindley haste; voices distinct, full Hooker letter missing. Invites publication while disagreeing on theory, urges caution and candour. Aquatic/glumaceous distribution, Eriocaulon route, Forbes African plateau, Cape zoology versus botany and Smyth report present as questions, hypotheses or attributed information. Ends mid-sentence. Darwin Must have been an island annotation is undated, not Bunbury body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1856: April 21, supplied 1856; all thirteen body blocks, ten notes and bibliography read. Answers April 16 Cape zoology question with tentative former-islands hypothesis, thanks Colletia update and quotes caution/candour advice. Gardener reply not received and not expected. P3 knows Lowe sent Porto Santo account, while Madeira flora only prospective; surviving Lowe copy read separately. Glacial interchange theory explicitly unproved synchrony, possible routes, speculative north-first cold and uncertain reverse migration. Confidential request is source prose. P13 directly addresses aquatic and glumaceous diffusion question; de Candolle longevity explanation disputed. Later June conversation is later witness, not date of current letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1871: May 9, supplied 1856; all three blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Thanks annotated list returned by Bunbury, whose full ninety-six entries do not survive in this web transcription. The surviving 1617 body is Darwin key, not incoming Bunbury prose; quoted Bunbury addenda in apparatus remain separate. Heer not yet read; August reading date later. Cold period cannot be proved geologically and is a probable explanatory hypothesis only. Raw 110 of means of dispersal is plain text with no MathML or fraction markup; preserve pending supported rendering repair. Reports three germinated seeds from earth enclosed in tree roots, distinct from pond-mud experiment; May 6 oral remarks not in published paper.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1852A: Additional Lowe April 12, 1856 witness; all eleven blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Original missing, contemporary copy by Lyell survives in scientific journal; no exact copying/receipt day inferred merely from April 13–16 visit. Porto Santo totals and overlaps use certain/doubtful ranges, include naturalised species and ecological limits; do not sum overlapping categories or flatten into exact counts. Madeira endemic estimate explicitly needs more research. Desertas plants and only freshwater eel reported, last spring capture qualified I believe. Original query only inferred from Darwin marginal note. Flora publication plan is apparatus/current other report, not a received finished book.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13784: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Conjectured March 20, 1855, based on Tuesday heading, diary and later conversation note. Thanks a missing Bunbury note and proposes Saturday morning talk before departure. Redirecting to Mrs Bunbury is a delivery arrangement, not evidence that she wrote the body or that the meeting already occurred. Footnote describes March 25 notes on flora; these are separate later witnesses. April 10 incoming 1664 answers a different missing letter of scientific questions, not this visit arrangement.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1664: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 10, 1855 incoming incomplete letter, four long surviving blocks. Explicitly answers unlocated Darwin questions about Cape mountain vegetation and Rubus distribution. Separates Zeyher reported observations, Bunbury personal recollections, estimated elevations, missing surveys, and hypotheses about aridity/wind. Myrsine distribution is a difficulty he judges unresolved under both migration and separate creation; do not convert it into Darwin agreement. Later Darwin cold-period annotations are undated, and later book citations do not establish April receipt. No direct reply or new exact knowledge date identified.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
